facts.statement: Jianchangnathus is an extinct basal pterosaur found in the Middle Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of northeastern China.
facts.quote: Jianchangnathus is an extinct genus of basal pterosaur from the Middle Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of northeastern China.

facts.statement: The genus Jianchangnathus was first described and named by Cheng Xin, Wang Xiaolin, Jiang Shunxing, and Alexander W.A. Kellner in 2012.
facts.quote: Jianchangnathus was first described and named by Cheng Xin, Wang Xiaolin, Jiang Shunxing and Alexander W.A. Kellner in 2012

facts.statement: The generic name Jianchangnathus combines a reference to Jianchang County with the Greek word for 'jaw'.
facts.quote: The generic name combines a reference to Jianchang County with a Greek γνάθος, gnathos, "jaw".

facts.statement: The specific name 'robustus' means 'robust' in Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name means "robust" in Latin.

facts.statement: Undescribed fossils suggest that the pycnofibers of Jianchangnathus were brown.
facts.quote: Additionally, undescribed fossils of a pterosaur referred to Jianchangnathus suggest that the color of its pycnofibers was brown.

facts.statement: Jianchangnathus is classified within the family Scaphognathidae, a classification supported by later phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: Jianchangnathus was assigned by the describers to the Scaphognathidae by the describing authors, which was corroborated by later phylogenetic analyses which included this taxon.

facts.statement: Jianchangnathus lived from the Bathonian to the Kimmeridgian stages, between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Kimmeridgian (168.2 to 152.21 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Spanish taxonomic record lists Jianchangnathus as belonging to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
The describers assigned Jianchangnathus to the subfamily Scaphognathinae.
facts.quote: Jianchangnathus fue asignado por sus descriptores a los Scaphognathinae.
